source_boundaries.web_review: Public text/sections listed under each source were actually opened and read on2026-10-15. Paraphrase only; no source code executed.
source_boundaries.book_review: Only Wiley excerpt printed pages13,15,17 sections listed below, not chapter3/full book.
source_boundaries.video_review: No video or webinar was viewed; an embedded player or lesson text is not represented as a watched video/transcript.

sources.title: TickVolume
sources.reviewed_scope: Definition, Remarks, and public C#/Python closed-bar examples only.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Tick volume counts ticks per bar. The example corroborates an existing price direction with an increase from the preceding bar; it does not use this repository's prior20 ratio.

sources.title: Understanding the CME Liquidity Tool Methodology
sources.reviewed_scope: Bid-Ask Spread, Cost To Trade/Buy/Sell and aggregation sections; text only, not formula images.
sources.reviewed_evidence: A missing bid or ask prevents a spread measure. Quantity-dependent trading cost consumes successive book levels; insufficient orders leave that cost unavailable. The 2024 methodology change is disclosed.

sources.title: Average True Range (ATR)
sources.reviewed_scope: Definition, Calculation and Using Absolute Value sections.
sources.reviewed_evidence: True range includes gaps from the preceding close. ATR measures magnitude rather than direction. TradingView defaults to RMA; absolute ATR values are not portable across differently priced securities.

sources.title: Repainting
sources.reviewed_scope: Historical vs realtime calculations / Fluid data values section; confirmed-bar alternatives.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Unclosed HLC changes during a bar; waiting for confirmation or using the preceding completed row delays the decision but avoids using fluid HLC as historical facts.

sources.title: Step 3. Risk Management and Your Trade Plan
sources.reviewed_scope: Accessible lesson text and risk-approach questions only.
sources.reviewed_evidence: A plan should set leverage, maximum trade/day loss, simultaneous positions and account exposure in advance. Published example percentages are examples.

sources.title: Jeff Quinto's Trading Plan
sources.publisher: Jeff Quinto, hosted by CME Group
sources.reviewed_scope: PDF pages 2 and 3 only: Risk and Goals; no full-document review.
sources.reviewed_evidence: The author's simulator plan pauses after three consecutive losses and specifies different holding treatment for winners versus scratches/losers. It supplies no twelve-bar wait, four-times-streak rule or calibrated survival estimate.

sources.title: Proper Position Size
sources.reviewed_scope: Accessible stop-first sizing explanation and contract/tick arithmetic.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Position quantity depends on a logical stop and predetermined account risk; loss per contract comes from stop ticks times tick value.

sources.title: The 2% Rule
sources.reviewed_scope: Accessible fixed-fraction examples and explicit arbitrariness statement.
sources.reviewed_evidence: The percentage is a chosen risk convention. A wider stop requires fewer contracts to keep the same cash risk.

sources.title: Probability calibration
sources.reviewed_scope: Sections 1.16.1 Calibration curves, 1.16.2 Calibrating a classifier, and class-presence caveats in 1.16.3.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Reliability compares binned predicted scores with observed positive fractions. Fitting a calibrator on a classifier's own training predictions is biased; Brier loss alone does not establish calibration.

sources.title: TimeSeriesSplit
sources.reviewed_scope: Class description and gap parameter, with gap=2 worked indices.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Splits preserve temporal order; gap removes a fixed number of rows before each test interval. Equal spacing is needed for comparable time duration. A row gap alone is not a trade-label overlap audit.

sources.title: Directional Movement Index (DMI)
sources.reviewed_scope: Description, How this indicator works, and Calculation sections.
sources.reviewed_evidence: ADX concerns strength; directional information belongs to directional movement components. The guide illustrates strong versus weak trend thresholds, which are not this runtime's qualified classifier.

sources.title: Exponential Moving Average (EMA)
sources.reviewed_scope: Description, trend/support interpretation and EMA recurrence.
sources.reviewed_evidence: EMA weights recent prices, lags turns and can change more often than SMA. Rising/falling EMA offers trend context rather than exact turning points.

sources.title: Introduction to trailing stops
sources.reviewed_scope: What is a trailing stop and distance tradeoffs; no broker connection.
sources.reviewed_evidence: A trailing stop follows favorable movement and stops retreating on reversal. Tight distances can exit routine pullbacks; loose distances give back gains.

sources.title: Chandelier Exit
sources.reviewed_scope: Calculation and interpreting sections only; text formulas, no spreadsheet/chart outcome claims.
sources.reviewed_evidence: Long level uses rolling high minus ATR buffer; short uses rolling low plus it. The daily22/3 illustration is not a validated M5 setting and its rolling level can fall as inputs change.

sources.title: Estimating univariate models
sources.reviewed_scope: Kaplan-Meier definition/fit, confidence intervals and durations/event-observed format only.
sources.reviewed_evidence: A fitted survival curve uses event durations and censoring. Kaplan-Meier multiplies one-minus-event/risk-set fractions and reports uncertainty; a deterministic age transform is not that estimate.

sources.title: Advances in Financial Machine Learning: official chapter-one excerpt
sources.reviewed_scope: Printed page13 pitfall table; page15 meta-layer FAQ and independent-data paragraph; page17 backtest-overfitting FAQ. No chapter3 algorithm or entire book reviewed.
sources.reviewed_evidence: The excerpt distinguishes side/size and meta-layer concepts, flags leakage/overfitting, and discusses later independent testing. It does not specify this repository's finite-bin estimator, training floors or threshold.

profiles.rule_math: ratio = current closed observed volume / mean(previous20 closed observed volumes); confirmation = available AND ratio > 1.2.
profiles.setup: An existing London trend-up normal-volatility candidate has a provider-identified activity series on its own timeframe.
operating_steps: Read the provider/unit and volume_available on each observation before interpreting activity. Tick count is not contracts, not notional volume and not order-book depth.
Require current volume>0 plus twenty prior positive available volumes. Shift before rolling; the current closed bar cannot inflate its own baseline.
Example: prior20 all100 ticks and current130 ticks gives ratio1.30. Bind only owner-published method_volume_available/method_volume_ratio and apply strict >1.2.
If confirmed, continue the original candidate through costs/risk; if unavailable or ratio<=1.2, WAIT. Record provider, bar close and baseline window.
Invalidate comparison on a provider/unit change or immature baseline. Do not claim increased ticks identify buy-versus-sell aggression.
inputs: method_volume_available:boolean from canonical availability and positive current/prior20 observations
method_volume_ratio:dimensionless
Underlying closed volume and volume_available, provider, unit and timeframe
wait_when: No genuine observed activity/availability or fewer than20 valid preceding bars.
Ratio<=1.2.
Provider or unit changes make the rolling comparison incomparable; preserve unavailable state.

alternatives.use: Closed price rise/fall plus tick increase over one preceding bar, matching the cTrader educational example.
alternatives.difference: Two-bar activity comparison has a different denominator and variance; it cannot be relabelled as the prior20 rule.

alternatives.use: Compare activity to the same time-of-session baseline when studying normal intraday activity seasonality.
alternatives.difference: Native seasonality normalization and its thresholds are distinct. Reuse its actual owner only when selected; no missing volume is backfilled.

alternatives.use: Exchange contract-volume corroboration on a homogeneous exchange feed.
alternatives.difference: Requires observed exchange contracts and roll/session definitions; present provider tick series cannot supply it.

profiles.invalidation: A price invalidation, loss of source availability, a new closed ratio failing the rule, or leaving frozen context ends this confirmation opportunity.
pitfalls: A high ratio can occur on a reversal; the original direction remains separately owned.
Mixing provider ticks with exchange volume creates a meaningless baseline.
A volume_lane=none NOOP is not proof that this method was used.
profiles.source_vs_lab: The cTrader source establishes tick units and a distinct two-bar corroboration example. Prior20, strict1.2, positive-volume availability and this context are repository hypotheses. No source or synthetic pass establishes profitable participation or agent skill.

Start a recognized new token atage0 and count actual subsequent observed rows. Example trend_up atages0,1,2,3,4 waits; the sixth same-token observation atage5 can pass.
The code compares raw lowercase tokens for age: trend_up to uptrend resets even though both map to+1. A synonym is not silently canonicalized for this counter.
Unknown tokens reset availability and the prior-token memory. A fresh recognized token after unknown restarts0; weekend clock time adds no observed rows.
